summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a right thigh abscess following two weeks of worsening pain, erythema, and swelling, accompanied by subjective fevers. She has a complex medical history including ESRD s/p deceased donor transplant, chronic immunosuppression, and prior MSSA infections. CT imaging revealed a large fluid collection in the anterior right thigh with hyperdense components, consistent with a superinfected resolving hematoma, not extending to deeper structures or the hip joint. She underwent bedside and OR incision and drainage, followed by wound VAC placement. Cultures grew MSSA, prompting a switch from vancomycin to cefazolin for renal safety. Her infection resolved with treatment, WBC normalized, and wound improved. She was managed for comorbidities including hypertension, diastolic heart failure, and CKD, with medication adjustments. Due to prior opioid-related respiratory depression, her pain regimen was simplified. She was discharged home with services for IV antibiotics, wound care, and follow-up, declining inpatient rehab despite recommendations.
